$comment: Preorder campaigns per Shopify SKU, read by app/lib/preorder-campaign.ts. Batches are in production order: a paid batch is stock Incutec already ordered and carries its own ship promise; any other batch is a funding target whose supplier order is placed once that many units are ordered. Set `ships` on a batch once its supplier order is placed. Only SKUs the Shopify catalog policy sells as preorder are affected. countFrom is the first day whose paid Shopify orders count. priceTiers is how the price steps per SKU as paid units come in, and a SKU may set its own priceTiers in place of it: upTo is the step's last unit and off its share off the Shopify compare-at price (the retail price). Past the last step a unit costs retail. app/lib/shopify-price-tier.ts writes each step to Shopify; a SKU Shopify still prices under its step closes until it is written. shipsBy is the one ship-by date of every funding-target unit, however early its target is reached. pendingShips is the ship promise for a funding-target unit: it must name endsOn and shipsBy; app/lib/preorder-campaign.test.ts checks both. A SKU's last batch has no end when it is a funding target: its units are the target, and once it is reached every later unit ships with it. endsOn is the target deadline, the end of that day in Europe/Brussels: a buyer whose target is missed by then chooses a refund or to keep waiting, and from then on a SKU whose next unit would wait for a funding target closes (paid stock and a batch with its own ships date keep selling). shipsWith lists SKUs that ship with a campaign SKU (accessories, spares): a flat Shopify price with no steps, units that do not count toward the lead, and the lead batch named in `batch` (one with its own ships date, or a funding target the SKU then waits for) or, without `batch`, the batch the lead's next unit falls into. With `stock` (units on hand) and `after`, the first `stock` paid units of the SKU ship with `batch` and later ones with lead batch `after`. Prices live in Shopify, never here. deliveryBy is the separately reviewed final customer delivery date for each batch; the ship promise names it, and null leaves it out. regions lists where a batch ships, EU, US or INT (absent: every region); paid stock is in Belgium and ships to the EU only, so it carries ["EU"]. Every paid unit takes the first batch with room that serves its region, the region being the order's shipping country (EU member, US, else INT): a US unit skips an EU-only batch for the next one that serves the US, and the batch counts, ship promises, paid-batch caps and batch tags all follow that allocation, while price steps and funding targets count every region. A SKU's last funding batch must serve every region. deliveryByUS is the reviewed delivery date for a US buyer (shipped direct by the fulfilment partner, duties included); a US promise names only it, and without it leaves the delivery date out. A shipsWith SKU pinned to an EU-only batch, or selling from stock, ships US units with `after` when that serves the US, otherwise with the lead's next US batch. usStock is what a US buyer's unit of any SKU not listed here follows (an in-stock item, a preorder outside the campaign): it ships with that US-serving batch of a campaign SKU, on the same promise, and Belgian stock stays EU only. deliveryByINT is the separately agreed arrival deadline for new international funding-batch orders. The usStock rule also serves INT accessories from the March batch. International shipping charges are confirmed by Shopify at checkout; no flat rate is configured here. US sales open only with PUBLIC_US_SALES and the rate in us-sales.json.
pendingShips: ships by 31 March 2027 if the target is reached by 15 December 2026, otherwise you choose a refund or to wait
